title: Rationalizing a geometric node over its finite separable residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], the base change $C_\Omega$ [def-pc-base-change] is empty or equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and every nonsmooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of $C_\Omega$ has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as a ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $x\in C$ be any nonsmooth point, with residue field $F=\kappa_C(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], equipped with its structural map from $k$. Then $x$ is closed in $C$ [def-weil-closed-points] and $F/k$ is finite separable [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Put $D=C_F$, and let $z:\operatorname{Spec}F\to D$ be the point induced by the residue-point map $\operatorname{Spec}F\to C$ and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Then $D$ is finite type over $F$ and has topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the point $z$ is closed, lies over $x$, and is $F$-rational (the structural map $F\to\kappa_D(z)$ is an isomorphism). For every algebraic closure $\overline F/F$, the point $\bar z\in D_{\overline F}$ induced by $z$ is nonsmooth and has $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D_{\overline F},\bar z}\cong\overline F[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as a ring.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), first proof, residue-field paragraph, expanded through Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family) and Morphisms Tag 02G7 (morphisms.tex, lemma-unramified-over-field). The dimension check is the affine base-change argument of the returned item, steps 1-4.

proof.text: Write $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$. The morphism $f$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field]. Choose the finite affine cover in the definition of finite type. Each coordinate algebra is finitely presented over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], since the only ideals of a field are $0$ and $k$, so $k$ is Noetherian. Thus $f$ is locally of finite presentation. The geometric-fibre assumptions are exactly those of [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular]: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point and its geometric fibres are the stated $C_\Omega$. That lemma gives $|Z|=$ the nonsmooth locus, $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ unramified, and the same support identification after every base change.

The point $x$ belongs to $Z$. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $x$, write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and let $\mathfrak p$ represent $x$, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. The algebra $A/I$ is finite type over $k$: the images of a finite generating set of $A$ still generate. Thus $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] to $Z$: $x$ is closed in $Z$ and $\kappa_Z(x)/k$ is finite separable. Moreover $\mathcal O_{Z,x}=A_{\mathfrak p}/IA_{\mathfrak p}$ has residue field $A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}=\kappa_C(x)=F$. The closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow C$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, so a point closed in $Z$ is closed in $C$. This proves both assertions about $x$ and $F/k$.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), applied to the singular subscheme of Curves Tag 0C59

proof.text: The residue-point morphism $r:\operatorname{Spec}F\to C$ and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ agree over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The fibre-product property defines $z:\operatorname{Spec}F\to D=C_F$ with projection to $C$ equal to $r$ and projection to $\operatorname{Spec}F$ the identity. In particular its image lies over $x$. At this image, the maps on residue fields are $a:F\to\kappa_D(z)$ and $b:\kappa_D(z)\to F$, with $ba=1$. Since a unital homomorphism between fields is injective, $b$ is injective; for $t\in\kappa_D(z)$, $b(a(b(t)))=b(t)$ implies $a(b(t))=t$. Hence $a$ is an isomorphism. On the chart above, $r$ sends $I$ to zero because $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so $r$ factors through $Z$; consequently $z$ factors through $Z_F$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), first proof, residue-field replacement, expanded by the fibre-product universal property

proof.text: By finite-type stability under arbitrary base change [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $D/F$ is finite type. The first-Fitting base-change identification in [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] identifies $Z_F$ with the singular subscheme of $D/F$. For every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/F$, associativity of fibre products identifies $D_\Omega$ with $C_\Omega$. Hence $D/F$ satisfies the same geometric-fibre hypotheses. It is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field] and locally finitely presented by the same finite-type-algebra argument as in step 1 (now over the field $F$). The nodal-family lemma therefore gives $Z_F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ unramified. It is locally of finite type, since on each affine chart it is the quotient of a finitely generated $F$-algebra. By [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] its point $z$ is closed in $Z_F$, and hence closed in $D$, since $Z_F\hookrightarrow D$ is a closed immersion. This does not assume $C/k$ separated.

Fix any algebraic closure $\overline F/F$. The morphism $z$ base changes to $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\overline F\to D_{\overline F}$ and, since $z$ factors through $Z_F$, $\bar z$ factors through $Z_{\overline F}$. The base-change and support clauses of [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] show that this point is nonsmooth. Under the canonical identification $D_{\overline F}=C_{\overline F}$, the structural embedding $k\to F\to\overline F$ makes $\overline F$ an algebraically closed extension of $k$. Apply the hypothesis at this particular nonsmooth point: $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D_{\overline F},\bar z}\cong\overline F[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as rings. No compatibility with a chosen coefficient-field embedding is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tags 0C59 and 0C5B, geometric-fibre condition and base-change singular support; Tag 0CBY residue-field paragraph

proof.text: Put $E=D_{\overline F}=C_{\overline F}$. The point $\bar z$ makes $E$ nonempty. Thus the hypothesis says that every irreducible component of $E$ has dimension $1$. To see $\dim E=1$ directly, take any chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $E$. Its largest member lies in an irreducible component by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], and the chain is a chain of closed subsets of that component, so its length is at most $1$. Conversely $E$ has a component (apply the same lemma to $\{\bar z\}$); since its dimension is $1$, it contains a chain of length $1$, also closed in $E$ because components are closed. Therefore $\dim E=1$.

source.place: Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension), dimension convention; elementary chain argument from pure dimension

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of the finite-type $F$-scheme $D$. The rings $B_i$ are finite type over $F$ by the finite-type definition. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the inverse images of the $U_i$ form an affine open cover of $E$ with rings $B_i\otimes_F\overline F$. The first (ring) assertion of [lem-pc-dim-base-change] applies to each $B_i$, with no integrality or algebraic-closedness assumption on $F$: $\dim(B_i\otimes_F\overline F)=\dim B_i$. Both $D$ and $E$ are nonempty, by $z$ and $\bar z$. Apply [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] to these covers, and identify its dimension with topological Krull dimension using [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings]. Equality term by term gives $\dim D=\sup_i\dim B_i=\sup_i\dim(B_i\otimes_F\overline F)=\dim E=1$.
